title: Specify flank finish against ISO 6336-22, not against a cost target

ideaData.title: Specify flank finish against ISO 6336-22, not against a cost target
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works (benchmark as named by the study): Lapped sets are cheaper and must be replaced as a matched pair. Ground sets are quieter, more repeatable and individually replaceable. The property that decides is micropitting resistance, which ISO 6336-22 exists to assess. SPEC: flank finish specified to an ISO 6336-22 micropitting assessment at the 4,400 N/mm* design unit load; ISO 1328 quality grade stated on the drawing; backlash 0.10-0.25 mm verified under load
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Cost effect (study): £0 — a specification, not a part. SPEC: flank finish specified to an ISO 6336-22 micropitting assessment at the 4,400 N/mm* design unit load; ISO 1328 quality grade stated on the drawing; backlash 0.10-0.25 mm verified under load
ideaData.riskNotes: Duty / environment: None. It removes a failure mode rather than creating one. Trade-off: Proven · effort Low. Trade: none. It replaces an argument about lapping cost with an argument about a measurable property, which is a better argument to have.
ideaData.powertrain: ICE / MHEV (longitudinal I6 ~500 Nm, V8 ~700 Nm, 8AT — study reference vehicle)
ideaData.targetVehicle: SCOPE: rear axle differential with an electronic locking differential, and front axle differential with an optional lock, for the reference vehicle in A1 (longitudinal I6 ~500 Nm, V8 ~700 Nm, 8AT rated 750 Nm INPUT, transfer case low range 2.93:1, final drive 3.54, 33-in tyres at 0.40 m rolling radius, 3,300 kg GVW, 3,500 kg braked tow, 900 mm wading, 240,000 km, EU plant, >=80,000/yr, 2026 prices). Covers the hypoid gear set, differential carrier and spider gears, locking mechanism, bearings and preload, carrier housing and cover, seals and breather, pinion flange, and assembly with backlash and contact-pattern setting. The half-shafts downstream and the propeller shafts upstream are separate studies. DIRECTIONAL should-cost, not a validated teardown BOM.
ideaData.studyCombinedCapture: COMBINED CAPTURE — honest, and NOT the sum. The saving cards add to roughly £81, and that number is wrong for four reasons. D1 is £29 of it and it is a brand decision, not an engineering one — three comparators have gone one way and four the other, and nobody here has written down which camp we are in. D4 is £18 and it buys the saving with 3 kg of unsprung mass on the front axle, which is the wrong direction on a vehicle sold partly on ride. D2 is £12 and it takes the driver out of the loop on a product sold on control. And P1 is conditional on M4 — alone it saves nothing. A realistic engineering-only capture, excluding D1, D2 and D4, is £15-19* gross; net of the M2 and P3 adders it is £4-8* on a £599 assembly, roughly 1%. That is the lowest engineering capture of the four studies, and the reason is structural: this assembly is castings, forgings and two bought mechanisms, with very little we can machine out. Add the RFQ at -12% and it becomes £76-80*. If the concept gate deletes the front locker and reverts the front housing to iron, add another £51 — but both of those are product decisions with real consequences, and neither belongs in a cost workshop.

title: Superfinish both gear sets

ideaData.title: Superfinish both gear sets
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works (benchmark as named by the study): Superfinishing reduces flank roughness, which raises the specific film thickness and pushes micropitting out. It also recovers a little efficiency at a mesh that slides about 125 m/min at 100 km/h, per Gleason. SPEC: both crown wheel and pinion sets superfinished after grinding; target micropitting safety factor to ISO 6336-22 stated on the drawing; measured axle efficiency improvement to be confirmed on a rig, not assumed
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Cost effect (study): +£8.20* — a cost ADDER. SPEC: both crown wheel and pinion sets superfinished after grinding; target micropitting safety factor to ISO 6336-22 stated on the drawing; measured axle efficiency improvement to be confirmed on a rig, not assumed
ideaData.riskNotes: Duty / environment: Re-validate on the durability schedule. It changes no duty case. Trade-off: Proven · effort Medium. Trade: it is an adder and the efficiency part of the claim is unmeasured. Buy it for micropitting margin and treat any efficiency gain as a bonus you have not yet earned.

title: Keep the breather and seal specification — refuse the saving

title: Net-forge the differential pinions and side gears

ideaData.title: Net-forge the differential pinions and side gears
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works (benchmark as named by the study): Eaton state that their ELocker internal gears are net-forged, providing the strength and durability needed for off-road use. Net forging gives grain flow along the tooth as well as taking cutting time out. SPEC: 4 differential pinions and 2 side gears per axle net-forged; gear-cutting time cut from 4.0 to 2.0 min rear and 3.5 to 1.75 min front; root strength verified at the 15,539 Nm* WHEEL design case
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Cost effect (study): -£6.05* net of tooling. SPEC: 4 differential pinions and 2 side gears per axle net-forged; gear-cutting time cut from 4.0 to 2.0 min rear and 3.5 to 1.75 min front; root strength verified at the 15,539 Nm* WHEEL design case
ideaData.riskNotes: Duty / environment: Re-validate. Root strength and grain flow both change, so the spider set is re-qualified. Trade-off: Proven · effort Medium. Trade: forging tooling amortisation at 80,000/yr, and the saving disappears if that volume drops.

title: Ground solid preload spacer instead of a collapsible spacer

ideaData.title: Ground solid preload spacer instead of a collapsible spacer
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works (benchmark as named by the study): A collapsible spacer is crushed at build to reach a rolling-torque target. The crush is irreversible: overshoot it and the spacer is scrap, and in the field a disturbed pinion cannot be re-preloaded without a new one. A ground solid spacer makes the build repeatable and the joint serviceable. SPEC: pinion preload set by ground solid spacer; rolling torque held at 1.5-3.0 Nm* on both axles, verified at 100%; spacer ground to 0.01 mm
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Cost effect (study): +£3.46* — a cost ADDER. SPEC: pinion preload set by ground solid spacer; rolling torque held at 1.5-3.0 Nm* on both axles, verified at 100%; spacer ground to 0.01 mm
ideaData.riskNotes: Duty / environment: PROTECTED LINE. It removes an irreversible operation from a 240,000 km assembly. Trade-off: Proven · effort Low. Trade: it is an adder and it will look like the wrong way round on a cost sheet. It is a warranty and serviceability purchase.

title: Replace the rear electronic locker with an automatic mechanical locker

ideaData.title: Replace the rear electronic locker with an automatic mechanical locker
ideaData.maturity: Proven — Eaton state the MLocker has had a long production run
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works (benchmark as named by the study): Eaton's MLocker is a self-contained automatic unit: it engages when a wheel-speed difference of 100 rpm or more is detected, locking takes less than a fraction of a second, it behaves as a light-bias limited-slip differential the rest of the time, and it is compatible with existing ABS and stability systems. SPEC: rear locker changed to an automatic mechanical unit engaging at a 100 rpm* wheel-speed difference; switch, harness, coil and control integration deleted; 5-10 A electrical load removed
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Cost effect (study): -£12.10*. SPEC: rear locker changed to an automatic mechanical unit engaging at a 100 rpm* wheel-speed difference; switch, harness, coil and control integration deleted; 5-10 A electrical load removed
ideaData.riskNotes: Duty / environment: Re-validate. The vehicle now locks when the mechanism decides, not when the driver decides, so stability-system interaction and on-road behaviour are re-tested. Trade-off: Proven — Eaton state the MLocker has had a long production run · effort High. Trade: IT TAKES THE DRIVER OUT OF THE LOOP. On a luxury off-roader sold on control, an axle that locks itself is a different product. And an automatic locker engaging on-road is a refinement event where an electronic one is silent.

ideaData.reviewOpenPoints: [MAJOR · quality] The figures and the stiffness claim do not follow from the stated inputs. 8.5 kg × £3.98/kg = £33.83 and 11.5 kg × £1.64/kg = £18.86, not '£57' and '£39'. The equivalent iron casting would be about 11.5 kg at £1.64/kg, costing about £39 against £57, and would be stiffer' Recommendation: Ask the author to show the £39/£57 build-up, and to support 'stiffer' with a deflection calculation at the stated mass.

title: Take the efficiency money HERE, not at the joints

ideaData.title: Take the efficiency money HERE, not at the joints
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works (benchmark as named by the study): The two hypoid drives consume 4-6% of engine power — the largest single efficiency line in the driveline. Half-shafts are about 1% and propshafts about 1%. The previous two studies both recommended AGAINST buying premium joints on an efficiency argument. This is where that money should go instead. SPEC: efficiency programme targeted at the axles: superfinished flanks (M2), oil level and churning depth optimised, seal drag and preload minimised; measured axle efficiency baseline established on a rig before any of it is committed
